text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nine people, members of two families, were killed in Boufarik, by two groups of "terrorists" who broke into their houses in attempt to abduct five young girls.
- Parliament, which has been revamped in record time, is ready to host the newly-elected 380 MPs on June 15.
- New MPs to hold first parliamentary session on Sunday amid intense consultations between National Democratic Rally (RND) and several parties.
- James Baker, United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara, says direct talks will take place between Rabat and the Polisario Front next week, in Portugal.
- "Terrorists" killed 12 members of two families and abduct five teenage girls.
- University entrance exams start in 29 provinces in northern Algeria.
- Ahmed Ouyahia is likely to be reappointed Prime Minister while Abdelkader Bensalah is expected to head parliament.
